error.no_credentials: No client certificate is set up. Add one in Settings → Apps → SmartThings Local.
error.credentials_required: Both the certificate and the private key are required.
error.credentials_not_persisted: Homey did not save the certificate. Try again, and restart the app if it keeps happening.
error.gateway_unreachable: Could not reach Samsung's gateway to look up the identity your appliances expect, so no certificate was issued. Check that Homey has internet access and try again.
error.not_recognised: This appliance is no longer recognised as a supported type.
error.wrong_device: {host} is a different appliance now: expected serial {expected}, found {found}.
error.not_writable: {capability} cannot be changed on this appliance.
error.no_remote_power_on: This appliance can only be switched off remotely, not on. Its own list of remote features offers power-off alone.
error.write_rejected: The appliance refused to set {capability} to {value}.
error.repair_no_device: Could not tell which device is being repaired.
error.already_paired: This appliance is already added to Homey ({model} at {host}). Open it from your device list instead.
error.handshake_refused: The appliance is refusing new connections. This usually clears itself within a few minutes; the app keeps retrying.
error.unreachable: Could not reach the appliance at {host}. The app keeps retrying, and searches the network for it by serial number.
error.setting_not_applied: The air conditioner accepted {capability} = {value} and then changed it back. This usually means it was still starting up — try putting a short delay after turning it on.
error.settings_conflict: The air conditioner would not hold these together: {settings}. Each was applied and then changed back by the appliance, which usually means the combination is one it does not allow — AI Comfort and a specific comfort mode, for instance. Pick one of them.
error.probe_no_response: Nothing answered at {host}. Check the address, and note that appliances older than about 2022 are cloud-only and cannot be controlled locally.
error.probe_no_dtls_server: {host} is reachable but has no local control port open. This is usually cloud-only firmware rather than a wrong address.
error.probe_handshake_refused: The appliance at {host} would not start a connection. That normally means it is still holding the previous one — wait a minute or two and try again.
error.probe_certificate_refused: The appliance at {host} connected but then answered nothing, which is what it does when it will not accept the client certificate. Issue a fresh one in Settings → Apps → SmartThings Local and try again.
